_metadata.description: Controlled vocabulary for the 30 drug-class identifiers referenced by interaction_rules.drug_class_rules. Splits into two tiers: 16 USER-SELECTABLE classes shown in onboarding/profile and 14 RULE-ONLY classes used by interaction rules but not surfaced as profile picks. v1.1.0 adds sheet-facing consumer-education fields (group_label, commonly_used_for) for the app's medication details sheet.
_metadata.purpose: Single source of truth for drug-class labels, brand examples, and prescription/OTC indicator. Drives drug-interaction warnings (e.g. anticoagulants + vitamin E high-dose → caution).
_metadata.alignment: Pipeline source: scripts/data/ingredient_interaction_rules.json `drug_class_rules[].drug_class_id`, scripts/data/clinical_risk_taxonomy.json `drug_classes`. Flutter consumer (user-selectable subset): lib/core/constants/schema_ids.dart `drugClasses` + `drugClassLabels`.

field_contract.id: Stable snake_case identifier shared with the user profile and interaction rules.
field_contract.name: User-facing label shown in onboarding and the profile screen (for user_selectable=true entries only).
field_contract.notes: ≤200-char plain-English description shown in tap-to-learn modal.
field_contract.examples: Common brand or generic medication names users might recognize on labels.
field_contract.rx_status: Prescription / OTC indicator. One of: rx_only | otc | mixed.
field_contract.user_selectable: Whether this class appears in onboarding profile picker. False classes are referenced only by interaction rules (CYP substrates, narrow families).
field_contract.group_label: Sheet-facing consumer bucket noun (e.g. 'Diabetes medications') shown as the classification label in the medication details sheet. Deliberately NOT unique: related classes share a bucket (anticoagulants/doacs/vitamin_k_antagonists are all 'Blood thinners').
field_contract.commonly_used_for: One plain sentence of consumer education for the medication details sheet, <=200 chars. Phrasing contract: starts 'Commonly used', never 'treats' (off-label reality, e.g. amitriptyline for migraine). Ships to the app verbatim after clinician sign-off.

consumer_copy_review.review_outcome: Round 1 (2026-08-08): 16 approved as authored, 14 approved_with_wording_change, 0 requires_revision. The 14 wording changes were applied and the packet regenerated; approval is against that revised copy.
consumer_copy_review.review_sources: MedlinePlus consumer monographs; FDA Established Pharmacologic Class labels
consumer_copy_review.note: APPROVED — these strings render verbatim in the medication details sheet. Any later edit to group_label or commonly_used_for invalidates this sign-off: reset status to pending_clinician_review and regenerate the packet (scripts/audits/drug_class_consumer_copy_v1_1/regenerate_packet.py) before repinning the Flutter asset again.

drug_classes.name: Blood thinners
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help prevent harmful blood clots, such as with atrial fibrillation or after a previous clot.
drug_classes.notes: Reduce blood clotting. Many supplements (vitamin E high-dose, fish oil, ginkgo, garlic, turmeric) further inhibit clotting and increase bleeding risk.

drug_classes.name: Antiplatelet medication
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help prevent heart attack and stroke by keeping platelets from clumping into clots.
drug_classes.notes: Block platelet aggregation. Combining with bleeding-risk supplements (vitamin E, fish oil, ginkgo) compounds the effect.

drug_classes.name: NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Aspirin regularly)
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help relieve pain, fever, and inflammation.
drug_classes.notes: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatories. Stack-with-supplement risks include GI bleeding (with fish oil, ginkgo) and reduced kidney function (with high-dose vitamin C).

drug_classes.name: Blood pressure medication
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help lower high blood pressure and reduce strain on the heart and blood vessels.
drug_classes.notes: Lower blood pressure. Some supplements (licorice, ephedra, high-dose caffeine) raise BP and counteract treatment; others (potassium, magnesium) compound effect.

drug_classes.name: Insulin or sulfonylureas (can cause low blood sugar)
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help manage blood sugar in diabetes; insulin is used in type 1 and type 2 diabetes, while sulfonylureas are used in type 2 diabetes.
drug_classes.notes: These medications push blood sugar down regardless of current glucose level, creating real hypoglycemia risk when combined with glucose-lowering supplements.

drug_classes.name: Metformin, Ozempic, etc. (rarely cause low blood sugar)
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help manage blood sugar in type 2 diabetes; some are also used for weight management.
drug_classes.notes: These medications work via glucose-dependent mechanisms and rarely cause hypoglycemia alone. Lower interaction risk with glucose-lowering supplements.

drug_classes.name: Not sure / other diabetes medication
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help manage blood sugar in diabetes.
drug_classes.notes: You selected diabetes medication but haven't specified which type. Tap to refine — your warnings will be more accurate.
examples: Please select Insulin/Sulfonylureas or Metformin/GLP-1 RAs above

drug_classes.name: Thyroid medication
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to replace thyroid hormone when the body does not make enough.
drug_classes.notes: Replace or modulate thyroid hormone. Iodine, kelp, soy isoflavones, and biotin can alter levels or assay results — separate by 4 hours from levothyroxine.

drug_classes.name: Sedatives / Sleep medication
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help with sleep or to ease anxiety.
drug_classes.notes: Promote sleep or reduce anxiety. Combining with supplemental melatonin, valerian, kava, or 5-HTP compounds CNS depression.

drug_classes.name: Immunosuppressants
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to reduce immune-system activity, such as to prevent organ transplant rejection or manage autoimmune conditions.
drug_classes.notes: Suppress immune response after transplant or for autoimmune disease. Echinacea, astragalus, and other immune-stimulating herbs may counteract effect.

drug_classes.name: Statins / Cholesterol medication
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help lower cholesterol and reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke.
drug_classes.notes: Lower LDL cholesterol via HMG-CoA reductase. Red yeast rice contains natural lovastatin and shouldn't combine; CoQ10 is often co-prescribed.

drug_classes.name: Antidepressants (SSRIs/SNRIs)
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help manage depression and anxiety; some are also used for nerve pain or other conditions.
drug_classes.notes: Increase serotonin (and sometimes norepinephrine) signaling. Combining with St. John's wort, 5-HTP, SAMe, or tryptophan risks serotonin syndrome.

drug_classes.name: MAOIs
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used for depression in selected situations; some MAO inhibitors are also used for Parkinson's disease.
drug_classes.notes: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors. Strict dietary restrictions (avoid tyramine-rich foods + supplements); many supplements are contraindicated or risky.

drug_classes.name: Other serotonergic medication
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used for different purposes, including depression, pain, migraine, and certain infections; these medicines share clinically relevant effects on serotonin.
drug_classes.notes: Other serotonin-affecting medicines such as linezolid, tricyclics, triptans, tramadol, buspirone, or meperidine. 5-HTP/SAMe can add serotonin risk.

drug_classes.name: Digoxin / Heart rhythm medication
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help control heart rate in atrial fibrillation and to improve symptoms in some people with heart failure.
drug_classes.notes: Affect heart muscle contractility and rhythm. Hawthorn, licorice, and grapefruit-related compounds can alter levels.

drug_classes.name: Anticholinergic medication
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used for conditions such as allergies, overactive bladder, motion sickness, or sleep problems; these medicines share anticholinergic effects.
drug_classes.notes: Block acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors. Combining with anticholinergic herbs (jimsonweed, belladonna) compounds dry mouth, constipation, confusion.

drug_classes.name: Anti-seizure medication
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help prevent seizures, and also for nerve pain, migraine prevention, or mood stabilization.
drug_classes.notes: Used for epilepsy and some pain/mood conditions. Several supplements alter levels via CYP induction or affect seizure threshold.

drug_classes.name: Antiarrhythmic medication
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help keep the heart in a steady rhythm.
drug_classes.notes: Stabilize heart rhythm. Several have narrow therapeutic windows and interact with grapefruit-related compounds, hawthorn, or motherwort.

drug_classes.name: Calcium channel blockers
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help lower blood pressure or relieve chest pain (angina); some also help control heart rate.
drug_classes.notes: Lower blood pressure and treat angina by blocking calcium influx. Grapefruit-related compounds raise levels of dihydropyridines.

drug_classes.name: Thiazide diuretics
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help lower blood pressure by moving extra salt and water out of the body.
drug_classes.notes: Increase urine output and lower blood pressure. Cause potassium and magnesium loss; supplements that further deplete or supplement these need monitoring.

drug_classes.name: Lithium
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help stabilize mood in bipolar disorder.
drug_classes.notes: Mood stabilizer with a narrow therapeutic window. Caffeine, salt intake, NSAIDs, and dehydration affect blood levels.

drug_classes.name: Oral contraceptives
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to prevent pregnancy, and sometimes to help with acne or irregular periods.
drug_classes.notes: Combination or progestin-only birth control pills. St. John's wort and some CYP-inducing supplements can reduce contraceptive efficacy.

drug_classes.name: CYP2D6-substrate drugs
drug_classes.group_label: Medications processed by the CYP2D6 enzyme
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used for many different conditions, from pain to blood pressure to mood; these medicines are all affected by how the CYP2D6 enzyme processes them.
drug_classes.notes: Drugs metabolized by CYP2D6 enzyme. Several supplements (St. John's wort, goldenseal) inhibit or induce this enzyme and alter drug levels.

drug_classes.name: CYP3A4-substrate drugs
drug_classes.group_label: Medications processed by the CYP3A4 enzyme
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used for many different conditions, from cholesterol to blood pressure to sleep; these medicines are all affected by CYP3A4 metabolism.
drug_classes.notes: Drugs metabolized by CYP3A4 enzyme. Grapefruit, St. John's wort, and many botanicals interact via this pathway and alter drug levels.

drug_classes.name: DOAC blood thinners
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help prevent stroke and blood clots, such as with atrial fibrillation or after a previous clot.
drug_classes.notes: Apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, or edoxaban; used for precise supplement interaction gates.

drug_classes.name: Potassium-sparing diuretics
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used for conditions such as high blood pressure, heart failure, kidney disease, or certain hormone-related conditions; these medicines tend to preserve or raise potassium.
drug_classes.notes: Spironolactone, eplerenone, finerenone, amiloride, or triamterene; potassium can accumulate.

drug_classes.name: Tetracycline antibiotics
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used for certain bacterial infections, including tick-borne infections, and for conditions such as acne.
drug_classes.notes: Doxycycline, tetracycline, minocycline, and related antibiotics; minerals reduce absorption.

drug_classes.name: Beta blockers
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help slow the heart rate and lower blood pressure, and sometimes for migraine prevention or anxiety.
drug_classes.notes: Nadolol and related beta blockers; green tea extract has specific nadolol evidence.

drug_classes.name: Fluoroquinolone antibiotics
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used for certain bacterial infections, including some urinary and respiratory infections.
drug_classes.notes: Ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, moxifloxacin, or ofloxacin; minerals reduce absorption.

drug_classes.name: Warfarin-type blood thinners
drug_classes.commonly_used_for: Commonly used to help prevent blood clots, such as with atrial fibrillation, mechanical heart valves, or after a previous clot.
drug_classes.notes: Warfarin and similar vitamin-K antagonists; vitamin K intake changes can destabilize INR, unlike DOACs.
